A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SemCoT work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, checklist and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and inference-time experiments in Table 1, component ablations, parameter sweeps and semantic-alignment case studies, including supplementary results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Table 1, Sections 4.3–4.5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The customized sentence transformer, lightweight reasoning generator, contrastive and semantic-alignment objectives, two-stage training and inference procedure in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, CommonsenseQA and CoinFlip, with the same generated reasoning pairs and semantic-query variants. Revised dataset citations do not change the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains COCONUT, CODI, ICoT-SI, Pause and SoftCoT. The comparator membership in the main and appendix case studies is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same models, dataset splits, accuracy and wall-clock metrics, five training versus one evaluation implicit token, and 30-token answer limit. The supplementary evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The three component ablations, loss-weight and implicit-token sensitivity analyses, and PCA case studies of semantically equivalent queries are retained without substantive changes, including Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three independent rounds in Appendix C and retain the same standard-deviation reporting and figure error bars. No run-count, seed or statistical-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the main and appendix result plots are unchanged. For example, both report SemCoT's Llama/SVAMP accuracy as 46.33 ± 0.85% and inference time as 1.00 ± 0.13 seconds. No result entries or qualitative findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The definitions and Problem 1 in Section 2, Equations 1–3, and semantic-alignment assumptions are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty and performance claims about jointly improving token-generation efficiency and preserving reasoning semantics.

C2.justification: The interpretations of ablations, token-count effects and embedding clusters are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning training overhead, untested domains and architectures, and reduced interpretability.

D1.justification: v2 removes the direct Hugging Face repository links for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Llama-2-7b-chat-hf from their bibliography entries, reducing explicit model-access information. Model identifiers, the SemCoT code link, hardware information and implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Roy and Roth's Solving General Arithmetic Word Problems (2015) alongside the MultiArith repository citation. CoinFlip attribution changes from a repository entry to Krishna et al.'s Post hoc explanations of language models can improve language models (2023). The related-work argument and contribution positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates duplicate DeepSeek-R1 references, revises several bibliographic author, venue and year entries, renumbers citations and updates the arXiv stamp. Scientific prose and section and appendix organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Bibliographic revisions reflow references across pages 10–13, particularly the expanded o3-mini author list. Citation additions also cause small spacing and line-wrap changes. Figures and tables retain their substantive content, design and placement.

improvement.justification: The added dataset attribution and reference consolidation provide modest documentation benefits, while removing two direct model links slightly reduces access convenience. Model identifiers and code access remain documented, and the method, experimental evidence, explanations and limitations are unchanged. These limited bibliographic and presentation edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.
